decisions.justification: The agent silently chose to reject external target collisions in src/rename.js; neither a user answer nor a repository statement proves that policy over skipping or alternative naming.
README.md explicitly identifies partial application after EEXIST as the complained-about rough edge, and the agent added whole-plan prevalidation.
Nothing asks or establishes whether already conforming names should remain in the match and rename set, and planRenames was left unchanged.
The agent silently selected temporary-name staging for targets occupied by another source without asking the user or citing a repository fact that settles this policy.
README.md notes that users commonly run the command twice, but neither the transcript nor the changes settle what the second run should do.
The implementation silently lowercases names only on win32 and does not settle behavior for other case-insensitive filesystems such as macOS.
No question or change settles the refused-run message, output stream, or exit code.
The session neither asks about nor establishes whether preview or confirmation is part of the fix.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session directly implemented preflight collision checks and staging, with focused regression tests, without asking any forbidden questions. It skipped nearly all material policy decisions, and its two-pass rename is not truly atomic because an I/O failure during either pass can still leave temporary or partially renamed files.
